newsitem.title: UK: Soft oils hold gains, palm oil lower in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Soft oils hold gains, palm oil lower in Europe.

text.p: Soft oils held their early gains at the close of the European vegetable oil market on Wednesday despite the lower Chicago opening.
Traders said the slightly easier dollar was enough to hold the market against the lower futures.
Palm oil drifted lower during the afternoon, but traders said there was unlikely to be much activity ahead of the PORLA report which is due out on Saturday.
Closer to home, some traders saw the possibility of tighter supplies of soft oils following the outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands.
"We could see a cutback in demand for animal feed which will lead to less oil being produced, but that is a long way down the road yet," said a trader.
The Dutch government said on Monday it would buy and destroy 800,000 pigs which cannot be marketed due to a ban on transporting livestock.
However, other industry sources said they did not think a cut in meal demand would make any difference.
"Most of the crushers are working to produce oil and although meal is very important, oil is their main consideration at present," said another trader.
Any cutback in demand for meal in the Netherlands would be short-term and would amount to around five percent of sales of animal feed to the pig industry.
At the close Dutch soy oil was 0.50 guilders up after Mar/Apr traded at 99.75 and 100 guilders while 102.75 guilders was paid for Aug/Sep.
Dutch/EU rape oil finished 1.75 to 0.25 guilders higher after May/Jul traded at 101.75 and 102 guilders per 100 kg fob ex-mill.
Crude palm oil closed $7.50 to $5 lower while products were $2.50 to $5 down.
Coconut oil attracted some dealer trading during the afternoon with Jan/Feb trading at $780, Feb/Mar at $772.50 and $770 and Mar/Apr at $762.50 and $760 a tonne cif.
Sellers were unchanged to $2.50 down by the close.
Palmkernel oil was $5 down and tradeless.
